The main purpose is to track how many copies are printed by each machine and compare them with the required quantity for each job. How the System Should Work Admin or designer will log in to the web portal and enter the job number, customer name, artwork details, machine, and required quantity. The printing machines should automatically send their live counter readings to the portal. The system should automatically calculate how many copies have been printed and how many are still remaining. Operators should be able to see the required quantity and printed quantity on their machine screen. When the required quantity is completed, the operator should know that the job is finished. If printing goes over the required quantity, the system should show an alert to prevent unnecessary printing. Main Features Required Central web portal with secure login for admin and designers. Connection with all 7 printing machines. Automatic machine counter reading and data updates every few seconds. Live dashboard showing required quantity, printed quantity, and remaining quantity. Search and filter by job number, customer, machine, and date. Overprinting alerts through email, SMS, or on-screen notifications. Daily production reports. Export reports in Excel and CSV format. Simple interface that is easy for operators and admin staff to use. Important Requirements Machine counter data must be collected automatically without manual operator input. Operators should not be able to change or manipulate production counts. Data should be accurate and updated in real time. The system should work reliably with all 7 printing machines. Final Deliverables Complete web portal. Machine connection software or utility. Fully working dashboard and reporting system. Source code and project files. Installation and setup guide. items.description: Hi, I'm building a SaaS for mountain tourism complexes and I need a developer (or a small team) to build the MVP. A mountain complex is one site with everything a mountain guest needs: hotel, chalets and huts, restaurants from valley to summit, gear rental, spa and sports, lifts, and transport. Most run each part on a separate system or on paper. A guest arrives by train, takes the shuttle up, rents skis, eats at the summit, books the sauna, and at checkout nobody has the full bill. When the wind closes the cable car, staff find out too late. The MVP has to prove one thing: one platform can run a full day of a mountain complex, put everything on one guest bill, and warn staff before the weather hits. I'll pilot it with 2-3 real complexes, then build the full SaaS on top. MVP SCOPE 1) Core - Complexes (tenants), buildings with altitude (hotel, chalets, huts, lift stations), outlets, staff roles - Winter and summer seasons with their own prices - Multi-tenant from day one, no self-signup (I create complexes) 2) Hotel - Rooms in different buildings, hut beds, season prices - Board plans (B&B, half board, full board) - Reservations, calendar, check-in / check-out 3) Guest folio - One bill per stay, every outlet can "charge to room" - Cash or card recorded (no gateway), split payment, printable invoice 4) Food, shop and rental - POS for restaurants and huts, knows which meals the board plan includes - Mountain gear shop - Rental: skis, boots, helmets, bikes, e-bikes, with sizes, deposit, return, damage fee 5) Hotel services - One booking engine for sauna, bath, spa, game room, sports, ski school and guided hikes: time slots, capacity, staff, price 6) Transport and lifts - Types: shuttle bus, taxi, car, bicycle, motorbike, lifts (cable car, chairlift, funicular, elevator) and external (plane, train, metro) - Own vehicles and drivers: schedules, routes on a map, bookings, no double-booking - Lifts: open / closed / on hold, lift passes charged to room - A guest's train or flight arrival creates a pickup 7) Weather (very important) - Forecast per building and lift station, because valley and summit differ: wind and gusts, snow or rain, fog, temperature - Limits per complex, warnings on affected lifts, trips and outdoor services - "Cancel for weather" that fixes the guest bills - Lobby TV screen: weather, lift status, avalanche level 8) Owner dashboard and reports NOT IN THE MVP: online payments, guest portal, lift gate hardware, real train or flight ticket booking,

items.description: I already have a working machine-learning model that detects sentiment on social media for Bank Mandiri, and I now need it turned into a full-fledged application. The goal is simple: pull posts from X (Twitter), Instagram, Threads, and TikTok, classify every entry as positive, negative, or neutral, and display clear trends and summaries on an interactive dashboard so non-technical stakeholders can see the overall mood at a glance. You will start from the existing notebooks and training data I provide, connect the relevant platform APIs, wrap the model in production-ready code, and create a responsive dashboard. I am comfortable with Python, so a stack that combines Python (FastAPI or Flask) on the back end with Streamlit, Dash, or a lightweight React front end would fit well, but I am open to alternatives if they speed development without compromising maintainability. Deliverables • End-to-end data pipeline that ingests posts from the four platforms in near real time. • Sentiment classifier that outputs positive, negative, or neutral labels with logged confidence scores. • Web-based dashboard showing daily and weekly trends, top keywords, and the current sentiment breakdown. • Setup scripts and concise documentation so the app can be deployed on our internal servers or a cloud VM in one step. Acceptance criteria • Accurate classification demonstrated on a held-out validation set I supply. • Dashboard loads in under five seconds with one month of data. • All services containerised (Docker) and runnable via a single compose file. If you have built similar analytics tools or have experience with the X, Instagram, Threads, or TikTok APIs, I would love to see your work. Let’s turn this prototype into a robust application that brings sentiment insights right onto our screens.

items.description: I need a small, purpose-built application that links my seven printing machines to a central web portal so I can see, in real time, how many copies have actually been produced versus how many were ordered for each artwork. Here’s how the workflow should look. Before a job reaches any press, either I or one of the designers will log into the portal and enter the required quantity. (The artwork’s file name already carries the job number and quantity, but I still want the definitive figure captured manually in the portal so there is no confusion.) Once production begins, each machine must push its counter data automatically to the same portal. As sheets roll off the press the portal should keep a running tally, display the remaining quantity for that job, and flag the operator if they begin to overrun. Because the updates are automatic, no operator input should be necessary at the machine; they should only see the live “required vs. produced” numbers on-screen and stop when the target is met. The portal needs a simple dashboard where I can filter by job number, customer, machine, or date and export a summary at the end of the shift to Excel or CSV. An alert—email, SMS, or an on-screen warning—is required whenever a job exceeds its assigned quantity so I can intervene quickly and cut wastage. Deliverables • Central web portal (browser-based) with secure login for admin/design staff • Machine interface or small utility that pulls the counter reading from each press and transmits it automatically every few seconds • Real-time dashboard showing required quantity, printed quantity, and balance for every active job, plus overrun alerts • End-of-day export (CSV/Excel) with totals per job and per machine • Installation guide and brief remote hand-off session so my team can manage new jobs without developer assistance If you’ve connected production equipment to a central tracking system before—whether through OPC, embedded APIs, or direct counter polling—let’s talk. My main priority is rock-solid data capture and a clean interface the operators cannot override.

items.description: I need a cloud-based GST compliance platform built specifically for a CA firm that handles multiple clients and registrations. The application must automate everything from data ingestion to final filing while remaining simple enough for non-technical users on both the firm side and the client side. Core workflow • Data capture: import sales and purchase data from Excel/CSV, accept invoices dropped into a browser-based client portal, and pull ledgers directly through the GSTN using an approved API. Manual file uploads from the portal must work interchangeably with the API so we can fall back whenever the gateway is down. • Return preparation & filing: generate GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B automatically, calculate GST liability and interest, and push the filings through our GST service-provider account. • Reconciliation: match purchase invoices with GSTR-2B, highlight ITC mismatches in real time, and let the user accept, reject, or flag items for follow-up. • Compliance tracking: calendar of due dates, status tracker for each client GSTIN, and colour-coded alerts. • Notice management: log departmental notices, auto-create response tasks, and trigger email/SMS reminders. Client-facing layer Clients log in to a branded portal where they can: – Upload invoices and supporting documents – Receive automatic reminders when data is due – View a concise dashboard of filing status, ITC position, and downloadable reports Firm-side dashboard Role-based access for partners, managers, and data-entry staff with drill-down analytics, workload allocation, and exportable audit logs. Tech expectations • Web stack of your choice (modern JS framework or Django/Laravel are fine) provided it performs well with large CSVs. • Secure multi-tenant architecture, 2-factor authentication, encrypted data at rest. • GSTN API integration and file-parser modules must be cleanly separated so we can maintain them independently. • Detailed documentation, unit tests, and a staging URL for UAT are mandatory. Deliverables 1. Source code in a private repository 2. Deployed SaaS instance on our AWS or Azure account 3. Install/upgrade guide and API keys wired up 4. Two rounds of post-launch bug fixes (30 days) Acceptance will be based on: successful filing of test returns through both API and manual upload paths, accurate ITC reconciliation against sample 2B data, and passing of our security review. items.description: # Fundraising & Strategic Investment Partner for XAVOT — Angels, VCs, Grants & Startup Funding ## About XAVOT XAVOT is an early-stage startup founded by Dushyant Kumar, a student entrepreneur from India. We are currently at the concept and validation stage, working to turn our vision into a focused, commercially viable venture. Our long-term ambition is to build an innovation-driven technology company focused on solving real-world problems through engineering, research, automation and deep technology. Our broader vision includes creating opportunities for students, innovators, engineers and companies to collaborate on real-world challenges and develop practical solutions. As an initial direction, we are exploring opportunities in the automotive sector, including real-world vehicle experience research, customer-driven product improvements and potential approaches to reducing vehicle manufacturing costs. These are areas under exploration, not validated products or proven cost-saving solutions. We are now looking for an experienced fundraising professional or strategic partner who can help us identify suitable funding opportunities and move from concept toward execution. ## Our Immediate Objective Our priority is to identify serious investors, suitable non-dilutive funding opportunities and startup support programs that match XAVOT's current stage, business direction and long-term potential. We are looking for someone who can do more than provide a list of investor names. If you have 5–10 years of hands-on Magento 2, PHP, MySQL and Linux experience, plus deep familiarity with AWS tooling, let’s talk through a roadmap and get the storefront performing at its best.

items.description: Every day I repeat the exact same sequence of clicks inside a web browser—open a site, sign in, navigate through a couple of pages, download a file, then trigger an upload elsewhere. I want a Python-based solution that takes this chore off my hands by reproducing each step reliably and quickly. Scope of work The script’s first responsibility is to handle those repetitive steps entirely in the browser. Selenium, Playwright, or a similarly robust library is fine as long as it can drive Chrome or Edge in both headed and headless modes. All credentials, URLs, and other variables must live in an external config (JSON, .env, or YAML) so I can adjust them without touching code. Any files created or fetched should be stored in clearly named date-stamped folders, and each run needs to leave behind a simple log so I know what happened and how long it took. Deliverables • Well-commented Python 3 script (.py) • requirements.txt listing exact versions • README that explains setup, config structure, and how to launch manually or via the OS scheduler Acceptance criteria 1. On a fresh Windows 10/11 machine with only Python installed, `pip install -r requirements.txt` completes without error. 2. Running the script reproduces the full click-stream in under two minutes and exits cleanly. 3. No credentials are hard-coded; they are read from the external config. 4. A log file named with the current date appears in the /logs directory after each run. If anything about the click sequence or browser choice needs clarification, let me know before you dive in so we can keep revisions to a minimum.
